title: Spanner: horizontal scale with transactions, and what it charges for

videos.script: AlloyDB had one writer. Spanner has as many as you pay for, and keeps the transactions anyway. {{writers}} It sorts every table by its primary key and cuts it into ranges of keys. Each range is served by one server, and Spanner moves the ranges as the load moves. {{splits}} So the key decides where the writes go. A key that counts up sends every new row to the last range, on one server. That is a hotspot. {{hotspot}} You will measure it on the emulator, against a UUID and a bit-reversed sequence, and see where new rows land. {{keys}} Then an order stored beside its customer, in an interleaved table. And a transaction that checks the stock and writes the order, all or nothing. {{transaction}} You will read the database as it was a few seconds ago, and watch the emulator refuse to run two transactions at once. {{emulator}} Last, what it charges for: nodes and processing units, three editions, and the smallest instance there is. {{bill}}
